summary: Special math functions and bit-exact RNG implemented through the real compilation path, with the two declared test files as the delivery. (1) Frontend: handlers for tl.exp/exp2/log/log2/sin/cos/erf/sqrt/sqrt_rn/rsqrt/floor/ceil (fp32/fp64 only, the pinned _check_dtype; 16-bit operands are located type errors), tl.abs (fabs/iabs/unsigned identity), tl.maximum/minimum (the propagate_nan policy carried BY the TIR op code: maxnum returns the other operand on NaN, maximum propagates a quiet NaN), tl.clamp, tl.fma, tl.div_rn, tl.sigmoid (the pinned 1/(1+exp(-x)) composition), tl.softmax (the SOFTMAX_COMPOSITE declared in plan/stages.py, replacing the old refusal stub), the explicit tl.add/sub/mul forms, and the RNG family: tl.philox as a new 4-result TIR op rng.philox plus the pinned random.py desugars for tl.rand/randn/randint and their 4x variants (counter=(offset_lo,offset_hi,0,0), key=(seed_lo,seed_hi), uint_to_uniform_float, Box-Muller). (2) Lowering/backend: the libm-backed vmath MIR op (per-element scalar calls to the declared sysroot's expf/logf/sinf/cosf/erff/floorf/ceilf and their double forms; -lm added to the link), vfsqrt/vfsgnjx/vnot/vmax/vmin/vmaxu/vminu/vfmax/vfmin/vmulhu/vfmacc/vmor repertoire rows, the NaN-policy compositions over vfmax/vfmin, the umulhi philox round expansion, the two declared fp64 internal-compute routes (i64->f64, f64->f32) plus the exact f32->f64 widening, and the pointer-select (where/ifexp between two pointers, the rng_dual target form). (3) Pre-existing defects found and fixed on the shared path, each with an executed reproduction: the vmath loop used the caller-saved element pointer after the PLT-clobbering call (wild store, guest SIGSEGV) and had used a callee-saved scratch corrupting the runtime caller (hang); the bf16 RTNE rounding added (bits>>1) instead of the LSB of the high half (first executed non-trivial bf16 rounding was wrong); the fcvt.fxu verifier rule was inverted (uint->float mis-rejected); strunc/swext rejected u64 sources; scalar widening kept the signed view for unsigned destinations; int widening/narrowing kept the source element kind for unsigned destinations; the vrgather group-footprint overflow in _int_narrow (odd-base SIGILL); region discipline was missing in the scalar-select, bit.invert, zeros/full, _mask_of_bool and scalar-convert paths (stale vsetvli in mixed-SEW passes); dtype == dispatch never folded (TypeObject/DTypeValue equality), routing fused_exponential into its dead 64-bit branch; tl.PropagateNan and x.dtype cast targets were not constexpr-foldable. (4) Validation: test_rng.py generates reference vectors from the pinned Triton 3.8 reference python (recorded with the generation command) and matches philox 128/128 words, randint/rand/rand4x bit-exactly, randn within tolerance; the off-by-one-round and wrongly-rounded-scale controls fail as required. test_math_ops.py executes all 20 declared math forms with 20/20 PASS, fp32 IEEE forms bit-exact vs the double-rounded oracle, fp16/bf16 through the fp32 lanes, integer abs/maxmin exact, NaN policies executed, located refusals for the fp16-transcendental and tensor-pow boundaries, the wrongly-rounded-constant control fails as required, and 1/2/4/8 threads share one artifact. Corpus operators executed and compared PASS: asinh_kernel, gelu_min, fused_activation, floor_kernel (math families) and all 5 compilable misc.rng operators (stochastic_ensemble, fused_fill_dropout, rng_dual in fp32/fp16/bf16, randint__randint, randint_like). The full existing test suite (26 files) passes with two stale expectations updated (softmax now lowers; mode_kernel now compiles). Compile-only sweep of the six families: math.transcendental 30/125, math.clamp 24/111, math.sqrt_rsqrt 18/62, math.round 1/7, arith.pow 5/15, misc.rng 5/12; every remaining refusal is a LOCATED diagnostic from another lane's declared boundary (tl.dot 24 operators -> T014; grid-model vocabulary 25; multi-axis partial reductions 58; early return 19; multi-width blocks 17; scalar record-width mismatches; case-without-kernel wrappers), not a math/RNG construct.
